tradeoff: Two workers hold a shared 4K HDR re-encode at 1.00x, but the longest freeze passed 2 seconds in 9 of 18 parts, all in the first 21 seconds after a first frame, on a machine at load average 5 to 33
decision: evidence; the 2 second bound is kept
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Play starts in seconds and keeps up.' 'Seeking and resuming just work.' Goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer.'
entry: Nothing is weakened: JS-168 merges with the miss recorded and docs/status.md carries it as an open gap. Accepting the long freezes as start-up (D) is rejected while no design around them has been tried and while the machine's load is not ruled out; holding back the first frame (C) is not considered until helpers at the start are measured. JS-174 enters at 18 beside JS-161 and holds no merge: on a quiet machine (or the dogfood under JS-166 if none can be had), two 2-CPU workers, 60 seconds from the start and 60 after a seek, 10 trials with and without burn-in, as built and with a helper asked for at the start and the seek for the measurement only; 2+6 at 5 trials. Met as built in 20 of 20: the gap closes. Missed as built and met with helpers at the start: that becomes a criterion of JS-161's shared admission. Missed both ways: a brief with C priced. JS-161 criterion 1 reads the figures if they are in and does not wait; JS-166 records the first 30 seconds' freezes apart. Unverified when decided: whether the freezes over 2 seconds come from load (2.25 to 3.0 s came at a load of 9 to 12; JS-167's quieter three-worker runs had 0.75 to 1.5 s); whether helpers at the start shorten them, since the first segment still comes from one worker; the dogfood's processors. Data that reopens it: JS-174's figures; JS-166's first-30-second freezes on the dogfood.
